verses.text: The LORD told me, “Go buy yourself a linen belt. Put it around your waist, and keep it out of the water.”
So I bought a belt like the LORD said and put it around my waist.
Then the LORD spoke to me a second time.
“Take that belt you bought, the one around your waist. Get up and go to the Euphrates. Hide it there in a crack in the rock.”
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, just as the LORD told me.
A long time later, the LORD said to me, “Get up, go back to the Euphrates, and get the belt I told you to hide there.”
I went to the Euphrates, dug up the belt, and pulled it out of its hiding place. It was wrecked, completely useless.
Then the LORD spoke to me.
“The LORD says, ‘That’s how I’ll wreck Judah’s pride and all of Jerusalem’s great pride.
These people are doing evil. They refuse to listen to me, follow their stubborn hearts, and chase after other gods to serve and worship them. They’ll end up like this belt, good for nothing.

I made the whole family of Israel and the whole family of Judah hold close to me, like a belt fits snug around someone’s waist,’ says the LORD. ‘I wanted them to be my people and bring me a name, praise, and glory. But they wouldn’t listen.’
“So tell them this: ‘The LORD, the God of Israel, says, “Every jar should be filled with wine.”’ They’ll say, ‘You think we don’t know every jar should be filled with wine?’

Then tell them, ‘The LORD says, “Watch. I’ll fill everyone in this land with drunkenness. That includes the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people living in Jerusalem.
I’ll smash them against each other, fathers and sons alike,” says the LORD. “I won’t pity them, spare them, or show them any compassion that would keep me from destroying them.”’”
Listen up. Drop the pride, because the LORD has spoken.
Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings on the dark and your feet trip on the mountains. You’ll look for light, but he’ll turn it into the shadow of death and make it pitch-dark.
If you won’t listen, I’ll cry in secret over your pride. I’ll weep bitterly, tears streaming down, because the LORD’s flock has been taken captive.
Tell the king and the queen mother, “Humble yourselves and sit down. Your crowns have fallen, those crowns you wore in glory.
The towns of the South are closed up, and there’s nobody to open them. All of Judah is being taken captive. Every last one is carried away.
Look up and see who’s coming from the north. Where’s the flock you were given, that beautiful flock of yours?
What will you say when he puts the people you trained to be your friends in charge of you? Won’t pain grip you like a woman in labor?
If you’re thinking, ‘Why did all this happen to me?’ it’s because your wrongdoing went so far that your skirts have been lifted and your heels have suffered violence.
Can an Ethiopian change their skin, or a leopard change its spots? If they can, then you who’ve gotten used to doing evil can do good too.
“So I’ll scatter them like bits of dry stalk blown off by the desert wind.
This is what falls to you, the share I’ve measured out for you,” says the LORD, “because you forgot me and put your trust in lies.”
So I’ll pull your skirts up over your face and let your shame show.

I’ve seen your disgusting acts: your adulteries, your neighing, and the indecency of your prostitution out on the hills. Jerusalem, you’re in trouble! You won’t get clean. How much longer will this go on?”
